data.title: Fizzing Volcano Lab
data.description: Discover the signs of a chemical reaction by mixing baking soda and vinegar to create bubbling fizz!

experiment.name: Baking Soda and Vinegar Reaction
experiment.realWorldConnection: This is similar to how baking powder helps cakes rise in the oven and how antacid tablets fizz in your stomach to relieve indigestion!

substances.name: Baking Soda
substances.safetyInfo: Do not taste or get in eyes. Wash hands after use.
substances.imagePrompt: White powder in a small glass bowl

substances.name: Vinegar
substances.safetyInfo: Avoid contact with eyes. Keep away from nose directly.
substances.imagePrompt: Clear liquid in a measuring beaker

reaction.particleDescription: When vinegar (acid) mixes with baking soda (base), their molecules break apart and rearrange, creating invisible carbon dioxide gas bubbles that rush upward and cause rapid fizzing!

challenges.instruction: Look closely at the reaction. What happened right after mixing the baking soda and vinegar?
challenges.targetAnswer: Bubbles formed rapidly and the mixture fizzed up
challenges.hint: Watch the beaker closely for escaping gas and foam.
challenges.narration: Fantastic observation! Those rushing bubbles are a telltale sign that new substances are being born!

options.text: The liquid turned bright neon green and turned solid
Bubbles formed rapidly and the mixture fizzed up
The mixture caught fire and glowed in the dark

challenges.instruction: Which specific signs told you that a chemical reaction took place?
challenges.targetAnswer: Fizzing, gas produced, and a slight temperature drop
challenges.hint: Think about what your eyes and thermometer told you.
challenges.narration: Spot on! Fizzing and gas production are absolute proof that chemical bonds rearranged into something completely new.

options.text: Fizzing, gas produced, and a slight temperature drop
Only a physical color shift with no bubbles
Loud music playing and a sweet smell

challenges.instruction: Is mixing baking soda and vinegar a chemical change or a physical change?
challenges.hint: Did it make brand new gas molecules that can't easily turn back into vinegar and baking soda?
challenges.narration: Brilliant work! This is a classic chemical change because the original reactants transformed into entirely new products like carbon dioxide gas!

observePrompts: What did you see happen immediately after mixing?
Did you hear any sounds during the experiment?

notebook.explainPrompt: Why do you think mixing these two substances created so many bubbles? What gas was released?
